I am a woman of 40 years here in Amhara, and I never went to school, but I know my land. This small plot of sorghum is only a tiny piece next to my bigger fields, so I cannot spend much cash on it. I will put the manure from my animals because that is what I always do, and I will plant the seed I saved from last harvest like my mother taught me. The rains will water it — I have no irrigation here — and my children and I will weed it ourselves without paying anyone.
